discovery: Silicon microstrip and hybrid pixel vertex detectors for precision tracking in particle physics

nominees.name: Erik H. M. Heijne
nominees.affiliation: CERN, Geneva, Switzerland; IEAP, Czech Technical University in Prague

motivation: Beginning around 1980, Heijne, Weilhammer and colleagues showed that planar-processed silicon microstrip detectors could measure charged-particle tracks with micron precision, first resolving charm decays in fixed-target experiments. Heijne then pioneered hybrid pixel detectors with bump-bonded readout chips, and Parker developed monolithic and 3D-electrode silicon sensors that extended speed and radiation hardness. These techniques became the vertex detectors of every major collider experiment. Silicon tracking made b-quark tagging possible, which was essential for the 1995 top-quark discovery at the Tevatron and the 2012 Higgs-boson observation at the LHC. It is now also used in X-ray imaging, medical diagnostics and space science. Few instrumentation advances have enabled as many fundamental measurements. Recognizing this one would honor the device physics and engineering on which modern discovery depends.
